title: Variables — practice quiz
description: A short check on Module 1. This quiz does not run GDScript; it only checks that the ideas landed.

questions.prompt: Which line correctly declares a fear meter that starts at zero in Godot 4 GDScript?
questions.explain: In GDScript you declare a variable with var. The := symbol tells Godot to infer the type from the value, so fear is a float starting at 0.0.

questions.prompt: What does @export do when you put it above a variable?
choices: It publishes the game to GitHub Pages.
It makes the variable show up in the Inspector so you can tweak it while testing.
It turns the variable into a constant that can never change.
It sends the value to a server-side sandbox.
questions.explain: @export surfaces the variable in Godot's Inspector. That is how you tune values such as max_fear or hear_distance without digging through the script.

questions.prompt: Which of these should be a const rather than a var?
choices: A fear meter that rises when a door slams.
A flashlight battery that drains while the light is on.
The maximum number of inventory slots, which should not change while you play.
Whether the flashlight is currently on.
questions.explain: const is for values that must not change. A slot cap is a good constant. Fear, battery, and a flashlight toggle all change as the game runs, so they are variables.

questions.prompt: You want a flashlight battery that starts at 100 and can later drop to 80. Which pair of lines does that?
questions.explain: Declare it with var and :=, then assign a new value with =. const would error if you tried to change it, and Godot 4 uses @export, not a bare export keyword.
